cards.back: AO1 assesses: technical control (accuracy, fluency, intonation), expression (dynamics, phrasing, articulation), and interpretation (stylistic understanding, communication).

cards.back: Minimum duration is 1 minute per piece — but quality matters more than length. A well-performed shorter piece can score higher than a poorly performed long one.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Choose a piece showing your STRENGTHS. Plan structured practice. Address technical AND expressive aspects. Demonstrate understanding of AO1 marking criteria.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Choosing a harder piece gets you more marks automatically. Correct: Marks are awarded for how WELL you perform, not how hard the piece is. A Grade 3 piece performed with excellent accuracy, expression and interpretation can outscore a Grade 6 piece with errors. Choose repertoire that demonstrates your BEST playing, not your most ambitious.

Select a solo piece appropriate for your ability. Explain your choice and outline a practice plan showing how you would prepare it for performance, addressing technical, expressive and interpretative aspects.
AO1 — Knowledge: Show knowledge of Solo Performance using appropriate musical vocabulary (e.g. terminology for elements, devices, and contexts).

Solo Performance is a key element of GCSE Music requiring theoretical understanding and practical application. The AQA specification requires you to identify, describe and analyse this element in set works and unfamiliar music. cards.front: Applying Solo Performance in Performance and Composition
cards.back: Understanding solo performance informs your performing (AO1) and composing (AO2) work. In performance, awareness of solo performance helps you make interpretive decisions that serve the music. In composition, solo performance provides the building blocks of your creative work — the choices you make about this element shape the identity and coherence of your piece.

cards.front: Exam Technique for Solo Performance Questions
cards.back: In the AQA GCSE Music listening exam, questions about solo performance typically ask you to: identify features by ear; describe how they are used; explain their effect; compare features between extracts. The key to success is precise terminology — never use vague language.
